relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: For the binding, select "bucket alias", specify **src\_user** as the "alias name" of the collection, select **bulk**, **data**, **users** as the associated keyspace, and select "read only" for the access mode. **Note we will not be using this binding as we have no need of it because we will use SQL++.**

notable_absence.finding: As in the Capella twin, no atomic or transactional cross-document consistency mechanism is claimed anywhere on this page - the cascade is implemented entirely by an OnDelete handler synchronously issuing an embedded SQL++ DELETE statement, filtered by a business condition (user_id >= 100) unrelated to any platform-level referential-integrity guarantee. The Server page adds one detail the Capella twin lacks any equivalent for: the binding it configures ('src_user', read-only) is explicitly declared unused - 'Note we will not be using this binding as we have no need of it because we will use SQL++' - showing the ADD FUNCTION dialog requires at least one binding to be configured even when the handler's actual data access goes entirely through an unbound SQL++ keyspace reference.

cross_product_finding: This page carries the same classic-role requirement (Full Admin / Eventing Full Admin via Function Scope, linking to eventing-rbac.md) documented across this whole batch's Server pages and absent from every Capella twin. It also notes a keyspace-naming migration fact with no Capella analogue: 'Note, the SQL++ keyspace of **bulk.data.transactions** in earlier releases would be simply the bucket **transactions**' - an on-premise upgrade-history detail tied to Server's discrete version history that has no meaning for Capella's continuously-deployed model.
